prompts.edges-v2: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent 2D sprite atlas for a side-view mushroom forest game. The supplied screenshot is ONLY a STYLE REFERENCE: match its hand-painted indigo intertwined roots, midnight blue stone, teal moss, restrained cyan edge highlights and deep black shadows. Detailed painterly game art, not photorealistic collage. No text, no scene background, no frame, no grid lines. No large mushrooms, runes, lightning cracks, jewels, buildings, detached props or long hanging vines. These are narrow surface skins on black solid terrain, NOT islands or pillars. Genuine transparent alpha around sprites and into the unlit interior. Make a 1536x1024 atlas, exactly FOUR HORIZONTAL ROWS (each 1536x256). One complete long skinny horizontal terrain edge per row, from x64 to1472, with 48px clear gutters above and below. Rows 1 and 2: FLOOR surfaces: level mossy TOP edge, dark thin braided roots and violet slate directly BELOW, material fades to transparency beneath within about 100px. Row1 braided roots; row2 fine slate intertwined with roots. Rows3 and4: CEILING undersides: dense narrow slate/root band ABOVE the level exposed BOTTOM edge, a few tiny downward root tips only, material fades to transparency upward within about100px. Row3 braided roots, row4 fine slate. Each strip maximum140px total thickness, very long and narrow, clear uninterrupted dark material band at the collision surface. Horizontal ends straight and quiet for tiling, no end-caps. Keep details small so it remains legible at 25px depth in game.
